ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a green quadrilateral. Inside the figure there is a dashed diagonal from the upper-left vertex to the lower-right vertex, labeled 18 in. The bottom side is labeled 21 in. A perpendicular line is drawn from the upper-left vertex to the bottom side, labeled 6 in. A perpendicular line is drawn from the upper-right vertex to this dashed diagonal, labeled 4 in. Then reason: Use this dashed diagonal to divide the quadrilateral into an upper and a lower triangle. The base and height of the lower triangle are respectively 21 and 6, so the area is (1/2)×21×6 = 63. The base and height of the upper triangle are respectively 18 and 4, so the area is (1/2)×18×4 = 36. Add the areas of the two triangles to get 63 + 36 = 99. The problem does not need further rounding.
